narrative.title: Subdividing the Stockroom Shelf Without a Calculator
narrative.scenario: A stockroom robot must split a shelf of length `dividend` into bays of length `divisor` — but its controller has no multiply, divide, or modulo circuit. It can only double and shift. The robot repeatedly finds the largest doubled divisor that still fits, peels that block off, and records how many such blocks each doubling step contributed, until the shelf is fully subdivided.
narrative.inputFormat: Two integers dividend and divisor (divisor is never zero).

complexity.optimalTime: O(log n) over the absolute dividend

testCases.explanation: Three full bays of 3 fit with a remainder of 1.
Opposite signs flip the quotient; 43 / 8 truncates to 5, so the answer is -5.

hintLevels: Level 1: Division is repeated subtraction — shifting just lets you subtract big doubled chunks at once.
Level 2: While the dividend fits, grow the shifted divisor b << q and bank 1 << q blocks per peel.
Level 3: Work on absolute values and decide the sign at the end; truncation toward zero, not floor, is the contract.
